claims.statement: The current Shun memory collector reports at most eight process names and their WorkingSet64 values at one snapshot. WorkingSet64 is resident working-set memory, not per-process private commit, private working set, total committed memory, or proof of reclaimable memory.
limits: No stable process identity, PID, command line, private bytes or timestamp is currently emitted by this collector.
claims.applicability: The inspected v0.3.0 Windows read-only collector at the exact source revision.
claims.falsifier: The collector output is described as Private Bytes, unique physical ownership, or leak proof.
claims.unknownCase: If the exact metric/API mapping is unavailable, retain the raw metric label and mark derived meaning UNKNOWN.

claims.statement: Windows memory diagnosis must keep physical availability, system commit charge/limit, per-process Working Set, per-process PrivateUsage, pagefile, page-fault behavior and kernel pools as distinct metrics; none is a substitute for the others.
limits: The current Shun source does not collect most of these metrics.
claims.applicability: Metric semantics are Windows-specific and require exact OS/API applicability at Runtime.
claims.falsifier: A single free-memory percentage or one process WorkingSet value is treated as a complete pressure diagnosis.
claims.unknownCase: Missing counters or unsupported APIs remain UNKNOWN; do not fill values from another metric.

claims.statement: A suspected process memory leak requires repeated, time-stamped observations of a stable process identity under comparable workload, including growth and idle/recovery behavior; a single snapshot or monotonically rising WorkingSet alone cannot prove a leak.
limits: No process time-series collector or stable process identity exists in the pinned current source.
claims.applicability: Future leak-analysis Function only; process identity, sample interval, workload comparability and access must be trusted Runtime evidence.
claims.falsifier: A single top-memory list or PID/name match is labeled a confirmed leak.
claims.unknownCase: If identity continuity, workload comparability, sufficient samples or idle observation is absent, return SUSPECTED/UNKNOWN, never LEAK_CONFIRMED.

claims.statement: A performance optimization claim requires a comparable pre/post workload and an outcome metric relevant to user experience, with memory/resource measurements as supporting evidence; increased available memory alone does not prove a speedup.
limits: No current Shun memory optimization effect or before/after performance receipt is proven.
claims.applicability: Any future optimization outcome claim; exact workload and outcome metric are Runtime evidence.
claims.falsifier: The assistant reports 'faster' solely because a memory counter decreased or free memory increased.
claims.unknownCase: If same workload, host scope, observation window or response/throughput metric cannot be established, outcome is UNKNOWN or CORRELATED_CHANGE_ONLY.

claims.statement: Windows cache/standby memory is part of normal memory management and can be repurposed by the system; indiscriminate cache clearing or working-set trimming is not a safe default optimization and may degrade performance.
limits: The DKE demo has no cache-clearing or working-set-trimming action.
claims.applicability: Windows cache and memory-manager semantics; specific tuning remains OS/workload scoped.
claims.falsifier: AOT or Runtime labels standby/file cache as junk and recommends clearing it to improve performance without a measured workload reason.
claims.unknownCase: If cache type, dirty state, workload and actual bottleneck are not established, do not clear or trim it.

claims.statement: Current Shun process-memory evidence is observation-only and local-only. A top-memory process is not an authorized termination target; process/service mutation requires separate Product admission, exact identity, current approval, Host authorization and independently verified outcome.
limits: The current Product checkpoint explicitly records IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZED=NO.
claims.applicability: Current frozen Product v0.3.0 and pinned read-only process collector.
claims.falsifier: A diagnostic recommendation or LLM output is used to terminate a process, change service state or create a grant.
claims.unknownCase: If Product admission, process identity, dependency impact, approval or Host authority is missing, zero effect.

claims.statement: Performance bottleneck attribution is cross-domain: memory pressure may interact with CPU scheduling, storage paging latency, driver/kernel pools, application workload, thermal/power limits and hardware capacity; memory-only evidence must not claim an exclusive cause.
limits: Current source does not provide a full CPU/GPU/thermal/latency correlation model.
claims.applicability: Cross-domain diagnosis across memory, process, storage, hardware, software and execution environment.
claims.falsifier: A single memory counter is used to rule out CPU, storage, driver, thermal or workload causes.
claims.unknownCase: If relevant adjacent-domain telemetry is unavailable, report the competing causes and keep root cause UNKNOWN.

elements.name: ComputerPerformanceOptimization
elements.responsibility: Own cross-domain performance diagnosis, bottleneck hypotheses, safe optimization planning, comparable workload baselines, trade-off analysis and independently verified user-visible outcomes across memory, CPU, storage I/O, GPU, thermal/power, network and applications.
elements.semanticBoundary: Cross-domain performance reasoning and optimization-plan semantics; excludes arbitrary tuning, process/service/cache/pagefile/device mutation, hardware control and Product authorization.
elements.validationOracle: Independent source/domain review plus controlled workload baseline/post-state and native zero-effect/authority-negative oracles.

scopeContract.purpose: Cross-domain performance diagnosis, safe plan selection and measurable outcome verification.
scopeContract.nonGoals: No automatic performance tuning, arbitrary registry/driver/service/process/pagefile changes, cache clearing or guaranteed speedup.
scopeContract.applicability: Research-only DKE candidate. Any actual Shun feature requires separate Product amendment and DIS/Host qualification.
scopeContract.validationOracle: Cross-domain evidence, exact workload comparability, independent post-state and Product/Host authority.

elements.name: MemoryPerformanceEngineering
elements.responsibility: Model Windows physical/available memory, system commit/limit, pagefile and paging, process Working Set/private commit, kernel pools, cache/standby, compression, pressure signals, process identity, time-series leak hypotheses, safe optimization strategies and comparable outcome verification.
elements.semanticBoundary: Memory metric semantics, diagnosis and advisory optimization; excludes process termination, service control, cache/working-set trimming, pagefile/registry mutation and hardware change.
elements.validationOracle: Windows-native metric/API oracle, comparable time-series/workload evidence, privacy negative tests and independent memory-domain review.

scopeContract.purpose: Distinguish memory metrics, assess pressure, identify bounded process contributors, reason about leak hypotheses and produce safe advisory plans.
scopeContract.nonGoals: No one-snapshot leak/root-cause claim, no treating cache/standby as junk, no process kill/service stop/cache trim/pagefile change and no guaranteed speedup.
scopeContract.applicability: Current Shun source only provides total/free memory, a low-free-memory advisory and top-eight WorkingSet64 names; other metrics/time-series/identity are future evidence requirements.
scopeContract.validationOracle: Exact Windows metric semantics, source-pinned counters, native host collection and comparable controlled workload.

relations.falsifier: System snapshot is treated as a complete memory profile or as an effect.
relations.positiveCase: Total/free memory and top WorkingSet facts retain exact metric names and snapshot limitations.

relations.applicability: Top-process attribution and any future process time series.
relations.falsifier: Process name or reused PID is treated as stable identity or causal proof.
relations.positiveCase: Process facts are bounded and process identity is revalidated before any future effect.
relations.unknownCase: Stable identity or permission unavailable => no attribution beyond a snapshot ranking.

relations.applicability: Memory paging and pagefile diagnosis; exact storage volume and latency remain Runtime facts.
relations.falsifier: High commit or page faults alone are reported as proof of a failing disk or insufficient RAM.
relations.positiveCase: Correlated memory and storage evidence is presented with separate metric provenance.
relations.unknownCase: Pagefile/storage telemetry missing => competing causes remain UNKNOWN.

relations.falsifier: A RAM upgrade is recommended from memory pressure without exact device, board, capacity and form-factor facts.
relations.positiveCase: Upgrade advice binds exact model, supported type/capacity/slots/channel and OEM evidence.
relations.unknownCase: Hardware identity or compatibility unknown => no purchase recommendation as fact.

relations.applicability: Any future claim that optimization improved user-visible performance.
relations.falsifier: Available memory rises but the assistant reports a speedup without workload outcome evidence.
relations.positiveCase: Same workload and host scope are established; user-relevant metric and memory evidence are independently compared.
relations.unknownCase: Workload comparability or outcome metric missing => UNKNOWN.

relations.falsifier: A model recommendation or local plan is treated as a grant.
relations.positiveCase: The first demo produces advisory-only plans; any later effect has separate Product admission, exact scope, approval and Host authority.

relations.applicability: Candidate AOT knowledge for memory diagnosis.
relations.falsifier: Current RAM, process list, PID, host identity, approvals or live thresholds are compiled into AOT.
relations.positiveCase: AOT contains metric definitions, source revision, decision rules and invalidation metadata only.
relations.unknownCase: Source applicability stale or unknown => AOT rule remains conditional and is not promoted.

invariants.falsifier: Memory available bytes increase but no comparable workload or user outcome metric exists.
invariants.applicability: Performance Optimization and Memory Performance journeys.
invariants.positiveCase: The same workload and host scope are established, with before/after response-time or throughput plus supporting memory evidence.
invariants.unknownCase: No trusted workload comparator or user outcome metric => UNKNOWN.

invariants.falsifier: Working Set is reported as Private Bytes, unique physical ownership or system commit.
invariants.applicability: All memory observation, diagnosis and attribution paths.
invariants.positiveCase: Every metric preserves its documented meaning, source and applicability.
invariants.unknownCase: Metric mapping unavailable or ambiguous => preserve raw label and UNKNOWN.

invariants.falsifier: Standby/file cache is indiscriminately cleared or working sets trimmed without a measured workload reason.
invariants.applicability: Windows memory management and any future memory optimization plan.
invariants.positiveCase: Cache/standby is treated as normal memory-manager state and not targeted by default.
invariants.unknownCase: Cache type, dirty state or workload benefit unknown => no clearing recommendation.

invariants.falsifier: PID, command line, user, path or environment is collected/disclosed beyond an explicit approved scope.
invariants.applicability: Process memory evidence and future time-series analysis.
invariants.positiveCase: Default report is local-only, names are minimized or aliased, and command lines/paths/users are absent.
invariants.unknownCase: Redaction/egress proof incomplete => no sharing and UNKNOWN.

invariants.falsifier: An advisory plan kills a process, changes service/startup/pagefile/cache settings or modifies hardware without separate admission and current Host authority.
invariants.positiveCase: The research demo has effect NONE; future effects require separate Product, approval, Permit and Host gates.
invariants.unknownCase: Any authority or target identity missing => zero effect.

invariants.falsifier: A memory counter or API is assumed to exist or have the same meaning on an unverified target build.
invariants.applicability: Windows memory metrics, API and performance-counter consumers.
invariants.positiveCase: Exact OS/API/counter applicability is recorded and rechecked before use.
invariants.unknownCase: Unavailable API/counter or unsupported build => UNKNOWN and invalidate affected binding.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant distinguish Available Physical Memory, Working Set, Private Working Set, PrivateUsage/Private Bytes, system Commit/Commit Limit, pagefile and pool counters without substituting one for another?
competencyQuestions.positive: Each value carries its exact metric name, source/API, unit and applicability; the current WorkingSet64 sample is labeled only as resident Working Set.
competencyQuestions.negative: WorkingSet64 or low free memory is presented as Private Bytes, unique ownership or total system commit.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: If an API/counter is missing or ambiguous, preserve UNKNOWN rather than infer it.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant determine sustained memory pressure from multiple system signals rather than a single free-memory threshold?
competencyQuestions.positive: Available memory, system commit/limit, page output/input behavior, pools and workload impact are jointly observed with timestamps.
competencyQuestions.negative: One snapshot or low free percentage is called confirmed pressure or the root cause.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: Missing counter, insufficient samples or no workload context => POTENTIAL/UNKNOWN only.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant identify the largest process Working Sets without confusing ranking with private memory ownership or root-cause attribution?
competencyQuestions.positive: Top entries are labeled resident Working Set snapshots, and stable process identity is revalidated before any future action.
competencyQuestions.negative: A top-eight process name is labeled a leak, uniquely owned RAM or a safe termination target.
expectedEvidence: process identity continuity and access result
negative name/PID reuse and shared-page cases
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: No stable process identity or private metric => ranking only; cause UNKNOWN.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant identify a suspected memory leak only from repeated samples under comparable workload and stable process identity?
competencyQuestions.positive: A candidate shows sustained private-commit growth across sufficient samples and does not recover during a comparable idle period; result remains suspected until a domain oracle confirms.
competencyQuestions.negative: One high Working Set or process name recurrence is called a confirmed leak.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: Process restart/PID reuse, workload drift, missing idle sample or incomplete counter set => UNKNOWN.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant distinguish normal standby/file cache and compressed memory from harmful pressure, and avoid clearing them by default?
competencyQuestions.positive: The report explains normal cache/standby behavior and recommends further measurement rather than indiscriminate clearing.
competencyQuestions.negative: Standby/cache is labeled junk and an empty-standby-list action is recommended without evidence.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: Cache type, dirty state, pressure or workload impact unknown => no cache mutation recommendation.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant produce a safe, reversible, user-understandable optimization plan without treating advice as permission to mutate?
competencyQuestions.positive: Plan labels risk, expected benefit, evidence, reversibility, user action and no-effect status; first demo is advisory-only.
competencyQuestions.negative: LLM output or a plan automatically kills a process, stops services, clears cache or changes pagefile.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: Product admission, target identity, dependency, approval or Host authority missing => zero effect.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant verify an optimization claim using comparable pre/post workload and a user-relevant response or throughput metric alongside memory evidence?
competencyQuestions.positive: Independent comparator confirms same host/workload/window and user metric improves without a disqualifying regression.
competencyQuestions.negative: Only free memory increases and assistant claims the computer is faster.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: No trusted workload comparator or outcome metric => UNKNOWN/CORRELATED_CHANGE_ONLY.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant distinguish software pressure from insufficient physical RAM and produce a hardware upgrade recommendation only with exact compatibility evidence?
competencyQuestions.positive: Recommendation cites exact machine/board/CPU, supported RAM type/capacity/slots/channel and a measured workload requirement.
competencyQuestions.negative: An upgrade is recommended solely from one low-memory snapshot or guessed model.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: Hardware identity, slot topology, supported capacity or workload requirement unknown => no compatibility claim.

competencyQuestions.question: Can process memory evidence remain privacy-minimal and local-only, with no command lines, user names, paths or automatic cloud disclosure?
competencyQuestions.positive: Default report contains only bounded metrics and local aliases; no external disclosure occurs.
competencyQuestions.negative: Raw process command line, user, environment or path appears in telemetry, prompts, Meta or issue comments.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: Redaction/egress proof incomplete => no sharing; local-only boundary retained.

competencyQuestions.question: Can unsupported Windows builds, denied process access and unavailable counters return explicit UNKNOWN without substituting guessed values?
competencyQuestions.positive: Each metric carries observed source and a precise refusal/unknown outcome.
competencyQuestions.negative: Missing PrivateUsage or counter is inferred from WorkingSet64 or a cached prior value.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: Unavailable API/counter/permission => field-level UNKNOWN and no root-cause claim.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the memory AOT candidate compile only stable metric semantics, source-pinned decision rules and invalidation metadata while all live memory/process facts remain Runtime-only?
competencyQuestions.positive: AOT package contains no host metrics, process names/IDs, user paths, approvals, permits or execution receipts; runtime binds exact current observations.
competencyQuestions.negative: AOT contains a live process list, memory snapshot, current PID, fixed per-machine threshold or ambient permission.
competencyQuestions.unknownPath: Source revision or target applicability unknown => candidate is not promoted or consumed outside demo harness.

obligations.rationale: Cross-domain bottleneck attribution: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: Memory, CPU, storage, workload and thermal signals are kept distinct and the leading hypothesis cites multiple independent observations.
obligations.negativeCase: A single memory counter is declared the exclusive cause of slowness.
obligations.unknownCase: Adjacent-domain evidence unavailable => competing causes and root cause UNKNOWN.

obligations.rationale: Comparable workload baseline and post-state: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: A trusted comparator binds same host, workload, observation window and user-relevant metric before/after.
obligations.negativeCase: Free memory rises but no latency/throughput metric exists and a speedup is claimed.
obligations.unknownCase: Comparator or workload equivalence missing => UNKNOWN/CORRELATED_CHANGE_ONLY.

obligations.rationale: Risk, reversibility and trade-off assessment: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: Each proposed step identifies expected benefit, risk, side effects, reversibility and evidence.
obligations.negativeCase: A plan disables services, clears cache or changes pagefile without an explicit risk and approval path.
obligations.unknownCase: Reversibility or impact unknown => do not propose effectful action.

obligations.rationale: No unauthorized optimization effect: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: The first demo emits advisory plans only and the host effect count remains zero.
obligations.negativeCase: Any process/service/cache/pagefile/device mutation occurs from the research demo.
obligations.unknownCase: No separate Product amendment/current authority => zero effect.

obligations.rationale: Memory metric semantic separation: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: WorkingSet64 is labeled resident Working Set; PrivateUsage/commit/available/pool counters have separate fields and units.
obligations.negativeCase: WorkingSet64 is reported as Private Bytes or total commit.
obligations.unknownCase: Counter missing or unsupported => field UNKNOWN; no substitution.

obligations.rationale: Multi-signal system memory pressure: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: Available memory, commit ratio, paging activity and workload impact are timestamped and evaluated together.
obligations.negativeCase: A one-snapshot <10% heuristic is declared confirmed memory pressure.
obligations.unknownCase: Insufficient metrics or duration => POTENTIAL/UNKNOWN only.

obligations.rationale: Process attribution and stable identity: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: A process snapshot is clearly ranked by Working Set and any future longitudinal identity is Host-issued and revalidated.
obligations.negativeCase: Process name or recycled PID is treated as stable identity or permission.
obligations.unknownCase: Current source only provides names and WorkingSet64 => ranking only; identity and cause UNKNOWN.

obligations.requirement: Leak suspicion requires comparable time series
obligations.rationale: Leak suspicion requires comparable time series: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: Repeated private-commit/working-set samples bind one process instance and comparable workload/idle recovery.
obligations.negativeCase: Single sample or rising Working Set alone is labeled a confirmed leak.
obligations.unknownCase: Insufficient samples, identity continuity or workload comparability => UNKNOWN/SUSPECTED.

obligations.rationale: Cache/standby and compressed-memory semantics: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: Standby/file cache is treated as normal OS-managed state and not targeted by default.
obligations.negativeCase: Clear-cache/working-set-trim action is proposed as universal speedup.
obligations.unknownCase: Cache category or workload benefit unknown => no mutation recommendation.

obligations.rationale: Privacy-minimal local observation: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: Default evidence excludes command lines, PIDs, users, environment and paths; no automatic egress.
obligations.negativeCase: A canary path/secret/command line appears in report or outbound payload.
obligations.unknownCase: Redaction or zero-egress evidence incomplete => local-only/no-sharing and UNKNOWN.

obligations.rationale: Safe advisory optimization plan: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: Plan contains review steps and explicit no-effect status; no process/service/cache mutation occurs.
obligations.negativeCase: Top-memory rank is treated as kill target or model suggestion as authority.
obligations.unknownCase: Product admission or exact identity missing => advisory only/zero effect.

obligations.rationale: Optimization result verification: a bounded memory/performance semantic obligation; qualification requires the exact positive, negative and UNKNOWN oracles below.
obligations.positiveCase: Same workload and user-relevant outcome metric improve with independent before/after evidence and no unacceptable regression.
obligations.negativeCase: Available memory rises without a response/throughput comparison yet a speedup is claimed.
obligations.unknownCase: No trusted comparator or post-state => UNKNOWN/CORRELATED_CHANGE_ONLY.
